core_classification.analysis: Erlend directly avows his continuing love for Kristin: “Gud vet at jeg elsker dig, Kristin.” The evidential frame “God knows” emphatically presents the loving state as true. Although spoken during an impassioned marital quarrel, it neither undertakes a new relational commitment nor appears as a reflex-like verbal discharge.
core_classification.ambiguity: The avowal also serves argumentative reassurance and self-justification, but these contextual purposes do not add performative or expressive/reflexive core force.

utterance_status.description: Erlend addresses his wife Kristin directly during their quarrel, embedding the love avowal under “Gud vet at” (“God knows that”).

contextual_interpretation: Erlend invokes his love concessively—he loves Kristin even while accusing her of being domineering and unforgiving. It counters her catalogue of his wrongs and helps justify his demand that old injuries no longer be held against him. His anger and movement away and back intensify the scene, but the wording remains a deliberate assertion within an argument rather than an affect-driven blurt. The surrounding passage independently portrays persistent attraction and attachment, without turning this particular utterance into a promise.

evidence.quotation_or_description: “Gud vet at jeg elsker dig, Kristin” (“God knows that I love you, Kristin”).
evidence.supports: The explicit first-person present-tense avowal, strengthened by an appeal to divine knowledge, strongly supports truth-conditional force.

evidence.quotation_or_description: Immediately beforehand Erlend tells Kristin that for him she will always be “den vakreste av alle kvinder, og den kjæreste” (“the most beautiful of all women, and the dearest”).
evidence.supports: This independently supports his presentation of an enduring affectionate state.

evidence.quotation_or_description: The avowal continues “endda jeg ser at du er herskesyk” (“even though I see that you are domineering”) and is followed by complaints about her failure to forgive him.
evidence.supports: The utterance functions as a concessive premise in an argument, not as an undertaking or renewal of commitment.

evidence.quotation_or_description: Before speaking, “Han gik fra hende og kom tilbake” (“He walked away from her and came back”).
evidence.supports: Despite the heated setting, the narrated pause and return provide no positive evidence that the words escape reflexively; they fit a purposeful argumentative avowal.

evidence.quotation_or_description: Membership review marks the occurrence KEEP with confidence 0.99 and reason “VALID_EXPLICIT_LOVE_I_YOU.”
evidence.supports: Confirms that the highlighted wording is an explicit love utterance rather than a merely formal or accidental string match.

ontology_assessment.diagnosis: T naturally captures the core avowal. The quarrel, self-justification, attraction, and possible pressure on Kristin belong to contextual interpretation; no important core force remains outside T/P/E.
